questions.question: What is immutability in String?
options: It cannot be modified after creation
The content can be changed at any time
It is only immutable in Java 8
It depends on the type of operation
explanations: Correct. Strings in Java are immutable; once created, their content cannot be changed.
No. Quite the opposite; the content cannot be changed after creation.
No. Strings are immutable in all versions of Java.
No. Immutability is a fixed characteristic; it does not depend on the operation.

questions.question: Which class is used to create mutable strings?
explanations: Correct. StringBuilder is the recommended class for efficiently building mutable strings.
No. StringBuffer also exists, but StringBuilder is faster in a single-threaded environment.
No. There is no StringMod class in Java.
No. There is no MutableString class in Java.

questions.question: How do you split a String into parts?
explanations: Correct. The split() method divides a String into an array of Strings using a delimiter.
No. There is no divide() method in String.
No. There is no separate() method in String.
No. There is no parts() method in String.

questions.question: How do you replace text in a String?
explanations: Correct. replace() replaces a character/string, and replaceAll() replaces using regular expressions.
No. There is no substitute() method in String.
No. There is no change() method in String.
No. There is no overwrite() method in String.

questions.question: How do you format a String in Java?
explanations: Correct. String.format() creates a formatted String, and printf() prints directly with formatting.
No. There is no sprintf() in Java; that is the C function.
